The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

One Beat for Beetle

BOM went Toad on the bucket. CLACK went Chip with two sticks. The Everybody Day band filled the garden with excellent noise. Caty saw Beetle put his little tapping stick away.

“What does your part sound like?” Caty asked him. Beetle took the stick out again. His feet did a cheerful wiggle. His stick did something Caty couldn’t hear at all.

“Louder!” called Chip, helpfully. Beetle hit the bucket as hard as he could. The stick sprang out of his feet. It landed in the soft feathers on Caty’s head.

Caty returned the stick. “Play it on your own wood,” she said. Toad stopped rubbing the dent in his bucket. Chip stopped laughing. Into that little pocket of quiet came tik-a-tik.

Caty tried a tune. “BOOM, clack, BOOM, clack.” Beetle waited politely through the whole thing. Caty scratched her cheek. “I seem to have used up all the places.”

She tried again. “BOOM, clack…” She held one wing in the air. Into the space came tik-a-tik! Bella’s tail jumped. “There you are!” she said.

This time Beetle started. Tik-a-tik, BOOM, clack. He played it slowly. He played it fast. Toad worked so hard to keep up that his bucket turned right over. It made a lovely final BONK.

Caty drew a drum for the Welcome Tree. Around its rim she drew a row of little beats and left a gap. If you held the paper leaf up to your ear, you could almost hear who fitted there.

Read together

Where would you leave a space in your song?
